# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 32 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 2

**1** Jesus said: "Let the one who seeks not stop seeking until he finds.

**2** And when he finds, he will be troubled.

**3** When he is troubled, he will marvel.

**4** And he will reign over all."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** P.Oxy 654 lines 5-9 preserves Greek parallel with a fifth stage: "and having reigned, he will rest" (καὶ βασιλεύσας ἀναπαήσεται). The Coptic lacks this. SOPHIA follows the Coptic.

**"Not stop seeking"** — EMET/LOGOS preferred over PNEUMA's "must not quit" — the more formal construction preserves the saying's imperative quality without over-colloquializing.

**"Troubled"** — all agents agree the middle stage must not be softened. PNEUMA's "shaken" is vivid but departs from the standard rendering of *šōrp*. "Troubled" retained.

**"Marvel"** — preferred over PNEUMA's "astounded"; the Coptic *šōrp* / *špēre* sequence implies graduated escalation.

**"Reign over all"** — consensus. The sovereignty promised is total.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Matt 7:7-8 / Luke 11:9-10 ("seek and you will find") — but without Thomas's troubling middle stages. Thomas's version is more demanding: finding is not comfortable but disorienting. Cf. also Matt 13:44-46 (the pearl and the treasure: finding requires everything).

**Textual Note:** The saying connects directly to Saying 1 — the "seeking" of Saying 2 IS the interpretive labor of Saying 1. The collection is self-referential from the outset.
